rows.verbatim:
The provision at FAR Clause 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors—Commercial Items is
applicable to this solicitation.
rows.normalized: Solicitation incorporates FAR clauses 52.212-1 through 52.212-5 (representative citation; full set spans pages 1-3).

rows.verbatim:
The factors are: Technical Capability and Functionality, Contract
Management and Customer Support, Speed of Delivery/Installation and Set-up, and
Past Performance.
rows.normalized: Government will evaluate offerors against four listed factors: Technical Capability and Functionality, Contract Management and Customer Support, Speed of Delivery/Installation and Set-up, and Past Performance.

rows.verbatim:
All evaluation factors other than price, when combined, are
significantly more important than price.
rows.normalized: Non-price evaluation factors combined outweigh price in award decision.

rows.verbatim: Each proposal must document the feasibility of successful implementation of the requirements of the SOLICITATION.
rows.normalized: Offeror's proposal must document feasibility of successful implementation of solicitation requirements.

rows.verbatim:
Offerors must submit information sufficient to evaluate their proposals based on the
detailed factors listed below.
rows.normalized: Offerors must submit sufficient information to allow evaluation against the listed factors.

rows.verbatim: Price evaluation will not be conducted on any Offeror determined to be technically unacceptable.
rows.normalized: Offerors found technically unacceptable will not have price evaluated (evaluation gate).

rows.verbatim:
Responses to this solicitation must include sufficient information to establish the interested
parties’ bona-fide capabilities of providing the product or service.
rows.normalized: Offeror responses must include sufficient information establishing bona-fide capability to provide the product/service.

rows.verbatim:
Responses to this solicitation must include clear and convincing evidence of the Offeror’s capability of fulfilling
the requirement as it relates to the government requirements stated in this solicitation.
rows.normalized: Offeror responses must include clear and convincing evidence of capability to fulfill the requirement.

rows.verbatim:
Basic cost and price information in the Offeror’s proposal must contain sufficient information
to allow the Government to perform a basic analysis of the reasonableness of the Offeror to
supply the required goods/services.
rows.normalized: Offeror proposal's cost/price information must contain sufficient detail for Government price-reasonableness analysis.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall submit its quote electronically.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit its quote electronically.

rows.verbatim:
Offerors MUST include a completed copy of the provision at 52.212-3, Offeror
Representations and Certifications Commercial Items, with their offer, OR provide a copy of
the valid certifications registrations and Representation and Certifications from the System of
Award Management (SAM) applications at www.SAM.gov, which may be indicated on the
Offeror’s cover sheet.
rows.normalized: Offerors must include a completed 52.212-3 provision copy with their offer, or provide valid SAM.gov certifications/representations.

rows.verbatim:
In addition the vendor Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and the certification of business size
must be included in the response.
rows.normalized: Offerors must include vendor UEI and business size certification in the response.

rows.verbatim:
All Offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM)
www.sam.gov.”
rows.normalized: Offerors must have an active SAM.gov registration.

rows.verbatim: All responses must be received no later than September 8, 2026, 12:00 pm EST.
rows.normalized: Offeror responses must be received no later than September 8, 2026, 12:00 pm EST.

rows.verbatim: Late responses will not be accepted.
rows.normalized: Late responses will not be accepted (evaluation gate).

rows.verbatim:
All responses must reference solicitation number
75N98026Q00960.
rows.normalized: Offeror responses must reference solicitation number 75N98026Q00960.

Responses must be submitted electronically to
3 scott.duernberger@nih.gov.
rows.normalized: Offeror responses must be submitted electronically to scott.duernberger@nih.gov.

scott.duernberger@nih.gov on or before 11:00 AM EST, September 2, 2026.
rows.normalized: Offerors must submit questions/clarifications electronically to the Contract Specialist by 11:00 AM EST, September 2, 2026.

rows.verbatim: Fax responses will NOT be accepted.
rows.normalized: Faxed responses to questions will not be accepted.

rows.verbatim:
Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the
Contractor shall furnish all the necessary services, qualified personnel, material, and equipment, not
otherwise provided by the Government as needed to perform the Statement of Work below.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish all necessary services, personnel, material, and equipment (not otherwise government-provided) to perform the SOW.

rows.verbatim:
The
Contractor shall provide preventative maintenance and on-demand repair services for Amnis image.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide preventative maintenance and on-demand repair services for the Amnis image instrument.

rows.verbatim:
Requirements include: • instrument software updates • preventative maintenance inspections, incl. one
(1) planned PM / year. • technical telephone consulting available during normal business hours •
unlimited on-site service visits when requested
rows.normalized: Contractor's service requirements include: software updates, one planned PM/year, technical telephone consulting during business hours, and unlimited on-site visits when requested.

rows.verbatim:
Contractor shall schedule and perform onsite preventive
maintenance from 8:00 am – 5:00 pm Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall schedule/perform onsite preventive maintenance 8am-5pm Mon-Fri excluding Federal holidays.

rows.verbatim:

make commercially reasonable efforts to obtain any required part within the targeted 48 hours of the
service technician assessment. 2. The service technicians need to be factory certified. 3. All services
provided under the Service Agreement will be performed in a workmanlike manner.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure: (1) commercially reasonable efforts to obtain parts within 48 hours of assessment; (2) factory-certified service technicians; (3) workmanlike performance of services.

rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide written progress reports during the period of performance.

documentation shall be provided by the vendor to show they completed service on the instrument and
should document technical progress with the POC.

notify the POC from the NIA/IRP for access to the subject equipment.

the products must conform to Section 508.

requirements of Section 508 or cite a justifiable reason for an exception.
rows.normalized: The contractor should state Section 508 compliance or cite a justifiable exception reason.

are less than fully compliant are offered pursuant to extensive market research which ensures that they
are the most compliant products and services available.

a compliant equivalent product or service, if commercially available and cost neutral.

rows.normalized: The contractor must follow government rules regarding confidentiality of information.

conform to the requirements of this contract.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall only tender for acceptance items conforming to contract requirements.

Governmentwide commercial purchase card), the Contractor may not assign its rights
to receive payment under this contract.

rows.verbatim:

contract, pending final resolution of any dispute arising under the contract.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall proceed diligently with contract performance pending dispute resolution.

The Contractor shall be liable for default unless nonperformance is
caused by an occurrence beyond the reasonable control of the Contractor and without its
fault or negligence such as, acts of God or the public enemy, acts of the Government in
either its sovereign or contractual capacity, fires, floods, epidemics, quarantine
restrictions, strikes, unusually severe weather, and delays of common carriers.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall be liable for default unless excused by causes beyond its reasonable control as listed.

rows.verbatim:
The
Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing as soon as it is reasonably
possible after the commencement of any excusable delay, setting forth the full particulars
in connection therewith, shall remedy such occurrence with all reasonable dispatch, and
shall promptly give written notice to the Contracting Officer of the cessation of such
occurrence.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall notify the CO in writing of any excusable delay's commencement and cessation, and shall remedy it with reasonable dispatch.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall submit an original invoice and three copies (or electronic invoice,
if authorized) to the address designated in the contract to receive invoices.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall submit an original invoice plus three copies to the designated invoice address.

rows.verbatim:
An invoice must include
(i) Name and address of the Contractor;
(ii) Invoice date and number;
(iii) Contract number, line item number and, if applicable, the order number;
(iv) Description, quantity, unit of measure, unit price and extended price of the items
delivered;
(v) Shipping number and date of shipment, including the bill of lading number and
weight of shipment if shipped on Government bill of lading;
(vi) Terms of any discount for prompt payment offered;
(vii) Name and address of official to whom payment is to be sent;
(viii) Name, title, and phone number of person to notify in event of defective invoice; and
(ix) Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). The Contractor shall include its TIN on the
invoice only if required elsewhere in this contract.
(x) Electronic funds transfer (EFT) banking information.
(A) The Contractor shall include EFT banking information on the invoice only if
required elsewhere in this contract.
(B) If EFT banking information is not required to be on the invoice, in order for the
invoice to be a proper invoice, the Contractor shall have submitted correct EFT
banking information in accordance with the applicable solicitation provision, contract
clause (e.g., 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer System for Award
Management, or 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer Other Than
System for Award Management), or applicable agency procedures.
(C) EFT banking information is not required if the Government waived the
requirement to pay by EFT.
rows.normalized: An invoice must include ten specified elements (Contractor name/address, invoice date/number, contract/line item number, description/qty/price, shipping info, discount terms, payee info, defective-invoice contact, TIN, and EFT banking info); 10 required contents in total.

employees and agents against liability, including costs, for actual or alleged direct or

Contractor is reasonably notified of such claims and proceedings.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall indemnify the Government against patent/trademark/copyright infringement claims, provided it is reasonably notified.

A proper invoice is an "Original" which must
include the items listed in subdivisions 1 through 12, below, in addition to the requirements
of FAR 32.9. If the invoice does not comply with these requirements, the Contractor will be
notified of the defect within 7 days after the date the designated billing office received the
invoice (3 days for meat, meat food products, or fish, and 5 days for perishable agricultural
commodities, dairy products, edible fats, or oils) with a statement of the reasons why it is
not a proper invoice. (See exceptions under II., below.) Untimely notification will be
considered in the computation of any interest penalty owed the Contractor.
1. Vendor/Contractor: Name, Address, Point of Contact for the invoice (Name, title, telephone
number, e-mail and mailing address of point of contact).
2. Remit-to address (Name and complete mailing address to send payment).
3. Remittance name must match exactly with name on original order/contract. If the
Remittance name differs from the Legal Business Name, then both names must appear on
the invoice.
4. Invoice date.
5. Unique invoice #s for all invoices per vendor regardless of site.
6. NBS document number formats must be included for awards created in the NBS: Contract
Number; Purchase Order Number; Task or Delivery Order Number and Source Award
Number (e.g., Indefinite Delivery Contract number; General Services Administration
number); or, BPA Call Number and BPA Parent Award Number.
7. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) which is in the System for Award Management
(SAM) and replaces the Dun & Bradstreet Data Universal Numbering System
(DUNS) number.
8. Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). In those rare cases where a contractor
does not have a UEI number or TIN, a Vendor Identification Number (VIN)must be
referenced on the invoice. The VIN is the number that appears after the contractor’s
name on the face page of the award document.
9. Identify that payment is to be made using a three-way match.
10. Description of supplies/services that match the description on the award, by line billed.*
11. Freight or delivery charge must be billed as shown on the award. If it is included in the item
price do not bill it separately. If identified in the award as a separate line item, it must be
billed separately.
12. Quantity, Unit of Measure, Unit Price, Extended Price of supplies delivered or services
performed, as applicable, and that match the line items specified in the award.*
